claims.claim: Origen of Alexandria was an early Christian theologian and biblical scholar, born c. 185 and died c. 253–254.
Origen was head of the Catechetical School of Alexandria and later founded the Christian School of Caesarea.
Origen delivered seventeen homilies on the Acts of the Apostles.
All that remains of Origen's homilies on Acts is a single fragment from the fourth homily, preserved in the Philocalia.
The Philocalia was a collection of Origen's writings compiled by Basil the Great and Gregory of Nazianzus, the Cappadocian Fathers.

The fragment from the fourth homily discusses how the Holy Spirit speaks through the prophets using prosopopoeia, addressing Peter's statement in Acts about Scripture being fulfilled that the Holy Spirit spoke through David concerning Judas.

Modern scholars including Jean Scherer, Pierre Nautin, Joseph W. Trigg, and Marcel Borret have challenged Eusebius's claim that Origen was over sixty before allowing his homilies to be recorded, suggesting they may have been recorded as early as c. 238 CE.
The fragment survives in Greek and is included in Migne's Patrologia Graeca.
